info.title: content-gateway
info.description: A gateway in front of the CurseForge and Modrinth APIs that holds the CurseForge key, caches answers for every consumer, counts the calls made on the key and holds every consumer off after a 429. `/v1/curseforge/{path}` mirrors `api.curseforge.com/v1/{path}` and `/v1/modrinth/{path}` mirrors `api.modrinth.com/v2/{path}`, answering their JSON as it came; `/v1/resolve` finds a download address per CurseForge file; `/v1/minecraft/*` lists Minecraft and mod loader versions from Mojang, NeoForge, Forge and Fabric, and the Java runtimes Mojang ships; the other routes are the gateway's own. Every route but `/v1/healthz` and `/v1/openapi.json` needs a consumer's bearer token.

get.summary: Each upstream's calls this minute per pool, its 429 hold, and its daily counts of the last UTC days.

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: UTC days to answer, today included, 1 up; 14 when left out, and more than the days kept answers the days kept.

400.description: `days` is not a whole number from 1 up

get.summary: What `GET api.curseforge.com/v1/{path}` answers, from the cache while it is fresh.
get.description:
The query string goes to CurseForge as it came, and the answer comes back with CurseForge's status, content type
and body, marked `X-Cache`. The routes of the cache table are kept for their fresh time; every other route is
asked each time. `Cache-Control: no-cache` asks CurseForge again and keeps the new answer. A kept answer that is
no longer fresh is still given, marked `stale`, when the budget refuses the call or CurseForge fails.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The path under `api.curseforge.com/v1/`, such as `mods/search` or `mods/238222/files`: segments of letters, digits, `-` and `_`

parameters.name: X-Budget-Pool
parameters.description: The pool the call draws from. Required when the token has more than one pool

parameters.name: Cache-Control
parameters.description: `no-cache` asks CurseForge again instead of answering from the cache

X-Cache.description: `hit` from the cache, `miss` from CurseForge, `stale` an old answer given because CurseForge could not be asked

502.description: CurseForge could not be reached or answered something the gateway cannot keep: `UPSTREAM_UNREACHABLE`, `UPSTREAM_TOO_LARGE` or `UPSTREAM_UNREADABLE`

503.description: The call was refused: `BUDGET_SPENT` this minute or `UPSTREAM_HOLD` after a 429 from CurseForge

Retry-After.description: Seconds until the next call can go out

504.description: CurseForge did not answer in time, `UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT`

default.description: Any other status CurseForge answered, with its body. Only the gateway's own answers lack `X-Cache`

post.summary: What `POST api.curseforge.com/v1/{path}` answers to this body.
post.description:
`POST mods` with only `{"modIds": [...]}`, `POST mods/files` with only `{"fileIds": [...]}`, and
`POST fingerprints/432` or `POST fingerprints` with only `{"fingerprints": [...]}` are answered per id from the
cache, and only the ids not kept are asked for, 100 per call. Every other body goes to CurseForge each time.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The path under `api.curseforge.com/v1/`, such as `mods` or `fingerprints/432`: segments of letters, digits, `-` and `_`

parameters.name: X-Budget-Pool
parameters.description: The pool the call draws from. Required when the token has more than one pool

parameters.name: Cache-Control
parameters.description: `no-cache` asks CurseForge again instead of answering from the cache

requestBody.description: The JSON body CurseForge expects at this path

200.description: CurseForge's answer, as it came, or one built from the kept rows of a batch

X-Cache.description: `hit` when every id was kept, `miss` when CurseForge was asked, `stale` an old answer given because CurseForge could not be asked

413.description: The batch needs more calls than a whole minute allows, `REQUEST_TOO_LARGE`; split it

502.description: CurseForge could not be reached or answered something the gateway cannot keep: `UPSTREAM_UNREACHABLE`, `UPSTREAM_TOO_LARGE` or `UPSTREAM_UNREADABLE`

503.description: The call was refused: `BUDGET_SPENT` this minute or `UPSTREAM_HOLD` after a 429 from CurseForge

Retry-After.description: Seconds until the next call can go out

504.description: CurseForge did not answer in time, `UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT`

default.description: Any other status CurseForge answered, with its body. Only the gateway's own answers lack `X-Cache`

get.summary: Whether the gateway is up, and which build it is.
A Java runtime Mojang ships with its launcher, from Mojang's list of runtimes kept an hour.
get.description:
`major` answers the newest runtime of that Java major, `component` the runtime of that name, as `javaComponent`
of `GET /v1/minecraft/versions/{id}` names it. The answer points at Mojang's manifest of the runtime, which lists
every file with its address, SHA-1 and size; the files themselves never pass through the gateway.

parameters.name: platform
parameters.description: Mojang's name for the platform: `linux`, `linux-i386`, `mac-os`, `mac-os-arm64`, `windows-x64`, `windows-x86` or `windows-arm64`.

parameters.name: major
parameters.description: The newest runtime Mojang ships of this Java major, such as 21.

parameters.name: component
parameters.description: The runtime of this name, such as `java-runtime-delta`, as `javaComponent` of a version names it.

400.description: `INVALID_QUERY`: no `platform`, or not exactly one of `major` and `component`

404.description: Mojang ships no such runtime for the platform, `UNKNOWN_RUNTIME`

502.description: Mojang could not be read: `UPSTREAM_UNREACHABLE`, `UPSTREAM_TOO_LARGE` or `UPSTREAM_UNREADABLE`

504.description: Mojang did not answer in time, `UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT`

get.summary:
A loader's builds, newest first: NeoForge from its Maven, Forge's promoted builds (the recommended and the
latest per Minecraft version, which is what pickers show), Fabric's loaders from its meta. `minecraft` keeps
only the builds for that version; for Fabric, whose loader is not tied to one, that means all of them when
Fabric supports the version and none otherwise. Each list is kept for an hour.

parameters.name: loader
parameters.description: `neoforge`, `forge` or `fabric`

parameters.name: minecraft
parameters.description: Only the builds for this Minecraft version, such as `1.21.1`.

502.description: The loader's source could not be read: `UPSTREAM_UNREACHABLE`, `UPSTREAM_TOO_LARGE` or `UPSTREAM_UNREADABLE`

504.description: The source did not answer in time, `UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT`

get.summary: The Minecraft versions Mojang lists, releases unless asked otherwise, newest first.
get.description:
`loader` keeps only the versions that loader has builds for, which is what a server or pack picker offers.
Mojang's manifest is kept for an hour and the old copy answers when Mojang fails.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: `release` (the default), `snapshot` (snapshots only) or `all` (every kind, old betas and alphas included).

parameters.name: loader
parameters.description: Only the versions this loader has at least one build for.

502.description: Mojang or the loader's source could not be read: `UPSTREAM_UNREACHABLE`, `UPSTREAM_TOO_LARGE` or `UPSTREAM_UNREADABLE`

504.description: The source did not answer in time, `UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT`

get.summary: One Minecraft version with the Java it needs, from Mojang's own document of the version, kept a day.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The version as Mojang names it

502.description: Mojang could not be read: `UPSTREAM_UNREACHABLE`, `UPSTREAM_TOO_LARGE` or `UPSTREAM_UNREADABLE`

504.description: Mojang did not answer in time, `UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT`

get.summary: What `GET api.modrinth.com/v2/{path}` answers, from the cache while it is fresh.
get.description:
The query string goes to Modrinth as it came, and the answer comes back with Modrinth's status, content type and
body, marked `X-Cache`. The routes of the cache table are kept for their fresh time; every other route is asked
each time. `version_file/{sha1}` is kept per hash and shared with `POST version_files`. `Cache-Control: no-cache`
asks Modrinth again. Modrinth needs no key but limits calls per address, so every call counts against the
Modrinth budget of the request's pool, and a 429 holds every pool off.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The path under `api.modrinth.com/v2/`, such as `search`, `project/sodium` or `version_file/{sha1}`: segments of letters, digits, `-` and `_`

parameters.name: X-Budget-Pool
parameters.description: The pool the call draws from. Required when the token has more than one pool

parameters.name: Cache-Control
parameters.description: `no-cache` asks Modrinth again instead of answering from the cache

X-Cache.description: `hit` from the cache, `miss` from Modrinth, `stale` an old answer given because Modrinth could not be asked

502.description: Modrinth could not be reached or answered something the gateway cannot keep: `UPSTREAM_UNREACHABLE`, `UPSTREAM_TOO_LARGE` or `UPSTREAM_UNREADABLE`

503.description: The call was refused: `BUDGET_SPENT` this minute or `UPSTREAM_HOLD` after a 429 from Modrinth

Retry-After.description: Seconds until the next call can go out

504.description: Modrinth did not answer in time, `UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT`

default.description: Any other status Modrinth answered, with its body. Only the gateway's own answers lack `X-Cache`

post.summary: What `POST api.modrinth.com/v2/{path}` answers to this body.
post.description:
`POST version_files` with `{"hashes": [...], "algorithm": "sha1"}` is answered per hash from the cache, keyed by
lowercase hash with unknown hashes left out as Modrinth does, and only the hashes not kept are asked for, 100 per
call, at most 1000 hashes. Every other body goes to Modrinth each time.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The path under `api.modrinth.com/v2/`, such as `version_files` or `version_files/update`: segments of letters, digits, `-` and `_`

parameters.name: X-Budget-Pool
parameters.description: The pool the call draws from. Required when the token has more than one pool

parameters.name: Cache-Control
parameters.description: `no-cache` asks Modrinth again instead of answering from the cache

requestBody.description: The JSON body Modrinth expects at this path; this shape for `version_files`

200.description: Modrinth's answer, as it came, or the versions found keyed by hash for `version_files`

X-Cache.description: `hit` when every hash was kept, `miss` when Modrinth was asked, `stale` an old answer given because Modrinth could not be asked

400.description: `INVALID_PATH`, `INVALID_BODY` (no hashes, more than 1000, or another algorithm), `INVALID_HASH`, `POOL_REQUIRED` or `UNKNOWN_POOL`

413.description: The hashes need more calls than a whole minute allows, `REQUEST_TOO_LARGE`; split them

502.description: Modrinth could not be reached or answered something the gateway cannot keep: `UPSTREAM_UNREACHABLE`, `UPSTREAM_TOO_LARGE` or `UPSTREAM_UNREADABLE`

503.description: The call was refused: `BUDGET_SPENT` this minute or `UPSTREAM_HOLD` after a 429 from Modrinth

Retry-After.description: Seconds until the next call can go out

504.description: Modrinth did not answer in time, `UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT`

default.description: Any other status Modrinth answered, with its body. Only the gateway's own answers lack `X-Cache`

200.description: The OpenAPI document of every route

post.summary:
A download address for each CurseForge file: CurseForge's own link, else Modrinth's copy of the file found by
its SHA-1, else the file's built address on CurseForge's CDN when a HEAD answers 200 with the file's size.
post.description:
The files are read from the cache like `POST /v1/curseforge/mods/files`, and the CurseForge calls for the ones
not kept count against the budget. Modrinth answers and CDN verdicts are kept for an hour, misses for 10
minutes. No bytes pass through the gateway: the consumer downloads from the address given. A null `source` with
`retry` false means no source has the file; `retry` true means a source could not be asked this time. At worst
a call takes 40 s: 10 s for CurseForge, 10 s for Modrinth and 20 s for the CDN checks.

parameters.name: X-Budget-Pool
parameters.description: The pool the CurseForge calls draw from. Required when the token has more than one pool

parameters.name: Cache-Control
parameters.description: `no-cache` asks every source again instead of answering from the cache

200.description: An address per file, in the order asked

413.description: The files need more CurseForge calls than a whole minute allows, `REQUEST_TOO_LARGE`; split them

502.description: CurseForge could not be reached or answered something the gateway cannot keep: `UPSTREAM_UNREACHABLE`, `UPSTREAM_TOO_LARGE` or `UPSTREAM_UNREADABLE`

503.description: The CurseForge call was refused: `BUDGET_SPENT` this minute or `UPSTREAM_HOLD` after a 429

Retry-After.description: Seconds until the next call can go out

504.description: CurseForge did not answer in time, `UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT`

ApiError.description: The JSON error every route answers with: `{ code, message }`, plus `pool` and `retryAfterMs` on a refused call.

message.description: What happened, in one sentence for a log line.

pool.description: The pool the refused call would have drawn from, on a refused call and an unknown pool.

retryAfterMs.description: When the next call can go out, on a refused call. `Retry-After` carries the same in whole seconds.

BudgetSnapshot.description: What `/v1/budget` answers: one budget per upstream, under one history and one source.

curseforge.description: The budget of calls on the CurseForge key.

historyDays.description: UTC days of daily counts the gateway keeps, the most `days` can cover.

modrinth.description: The budget of calls to Modrinth, which rate-limits the gateway's address.

DayCounts.description: What one pool did on one UTC day.

hits.description: Requests answered without a call: from the cache, or by joining a call already in flight.

DayPoolSnapshot.description: One pool's counts on one UTC day.

DaySnapshot.description: One UTC day's counts for every pool.

ErrorCode.description: What went wrong, for a consumer to branch on.

FileSource.description: Where a file's download address comes from.

Health.description: What `/v1/healthz` answers: the running gateway's version and build.

builtAt.description: When the binary was built, ISO 8601 in UTC, when the build said.

commit.description: The commit the binary was built from, when the build said.

status.description: Always `ok` when the gateway answers at all.

JavaRuntime.description: What `GET /v1/minecraft/java` answers: one Java runtime Mojang ships for a platform.

released.description: When Mojang released this build of the runtime, ISO 8601, or null when Mojang does not say.

version.description: The Java version Mojang lists, such as `21.0.7` or `8u202`.

Latest.description: The newest release and snapshot Mojang names, whatever the filter.

Loader.description: The mod loaders whose versions the gateway lists.

minecraft.description: The Minecraft version the build is for; null for Fabric, whose loader works with every version it supports.

recommended.description: True for the build its maintainers recommend for the Minecraft version, where they say.

stable.description: False for a beta or pre-release build.

minecraft.description: The Minecraft version the list was narrowed to, or null for every build.

MinecraftVersion.description: One Minecraft version as Mojang's manifest lists it.

MinecraftVersionDetails.description: What `GET /v1/minecraft/versions/{id}` answers: the version and the Java it needs.

javaComponent.description: Mojang's runtime for it, such as `java-runtime-delta`, the `component` of `GET /v1/minecraft/java`; null when Mojang does not say.

javaMajor.description: The major version of the Java the version runs on, such as 21, or null when Mojang does not say.

versions.description: Newest first, as Mojang lists them.

cdn.description:
Whether a file's built address on CurseForge's CDN may be checked and given when neither CurseForge nor
Modrinth has a link. On unless set to false.

files.description: One entry per file id asked for, in the order asked, each id once.

ResolvedFile.description: What `POST /v1/resolve` answers for each file asked for.

fileName.description: The file's name as CurseForge lists it, null when CurseForge does not know the file.

retry.description:
True when a source could not be asked for the file, so that a null `source` is worth asking again later
rather than remembering.

sha1.description: The file's SHA-1 as CurseForge lists it, null when CurseForge does not know the file.

size.description: The file's size in bytes as CurseForge lists it, null when CurseForge does not know the file.

oneOf.description: Where `url` comes from, or null when no source has the file.

url.description: The address to download the file from, or null when no source has it.

RuntimeManifest.description: Mojang's manifest of a runtime: every file to download, with its address, SHA-1 and size.

sha1.description: The SHA-1 of the manifest itself.

size.description: The size of the manifest in bytes.

Source.description:
Where a readout's counts come from: `redis` when they are the stored ones, `memory` when no Redis is configured,
`unavailable` when Redis did not answer, so the minute is this process's own count and the days hold only what
is not written to Redis yet.

UpstreamBudget.description: One upstream's budget: this minute over all pools and per pool, the 429 hold, and the last UTC days.

days.description: The UTC days asked for, today first; a day without a single count is left out.

heldUntil.description: Until when the upstream's 429 holds every call off, ISO 8601, or null while no hold is on.

limitPerMinute.description: Calls the minute allows over all pools.

pools.description: Every pool of every consumer, this minute.

resetsAt.description: When this minute's counts start over, ISO 8601.

hashes.description: SHA-1 hashes of the wanted files, 40 hex digits each, up to 1000.

bearer.description: A consumer's token, from the gateway's configuration

tags.name: minecraft
tags.description: Minecraft and mod loader version lists, and Mojang's Java runtimes
